title: Local Exploitation of MSKSSRV Kernel Vulnerability CVE-2024-35250
id: 4d61e4d1-3abf-4f94-8c1a-7142c995c682
status: experimental
description: Detects exploitation attempts of CVE-2024-35250 in MSKSSRV driver using IOCTL_KS_PROPERTY with KSPROPERTY_TYPE_UNSERIALIZESET flag.
references:
    - https://thehackernews.com/2024/12/cisa-and-fbi-raise-alerts-on-exploited.html

author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-09-24
tags:
    - attack.privilege_escalation
    - attack.t1068

    category: process_creation
    product: windows

falsepositives:

pipeline.attack_summary: An attacker uses phishing emails containing malicious links to deliver a NetWire RAT variant. The initial payload is a Word document with macros that download GuLoader, which then retrieves and executes the NetWire RAT. The malware establishes persistence via registry keys, collects system information, logs keystrokes, and communicates with a C2 server using DNS resolution for IP address discovery.

NetWire is a Remote Access Trojan(RAT) malware that has been widely used for many years. Recently, FortiGuard Labs noticed a type of malware spreading via phishing email, and during the analysis of it, we discovered that it was a new variant of NetWire RAT.
GuLoader is a file downloader that was first discovered in December 2019, and it has been used to distribute a wide variety of remote administration tool (RAT) malware.

status: experimental
description: Detects unauthenticated HTTP POST requests to the WSUS ReportingWebService endpoint with specially crafted SOAP payload triggering unsafe deserialization of AuthorizationCookie via SynchronizationUpdateErrorsKey field.
references:
    - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/microsoft-cve-2025-59287/
    - https://www.huntress.com/blog/exploitation-of-windows-server-update-services-remote-code-execution-vulnerability

date: 2026-09-24

    category: webserver
    product: windows/iis
detection:

Analysis and Report by Fabian Marquardt (@marqufabi) - Recently, Telekom Security CTI was made aware via trust groups in which we are engaged about a new malware campaign that is distributed via phishing emails. The malspam campaign used stolen email threads to lure victim users into clicking the contained hyperlink, which downloaded the malware. Attention to this malware campaign was also fueled by a false attribution of one of the malware samples to Emotet. Even though this attribution later turned out as a false positive match of an automated detection rule, it caused the security research community to focus on this new campaign. Initial analysis quickly revealed significant similarity to the DarkGate malware, based on the use of a similar initial infection routine (AutoIt scripts) and the observed C2 communication protocol, which matched past analyses of the same malware family.

The script can be decompiled using myAut2Exe (a pre-compiled binary can be found here) after renaming the file from .au3 to .a3x. Analysis of the decompiled script shows that the sole purpose of the script is to execute a shellcode that is contained as a hex-encoded string: The screenshot above only shows an excerpt of the complete sequence to create the shellcode string. This string is then decoded to binary data and written to a newly allocated memory area using the BinaryToString and DllStructCreate function calls. Finally, two commands are executed. These commands are obfuscated as hex-encoded strings. Decoding these strings reveals their purpose, which is to make the newly allocated memory area executable with VirtualProtect and call the shellcode using CallWindowProc:

pipeline.attack_summary: Kapeka is a novel backdoor used by the Russian nation-state group Sandworm since at least mid-2022, likely deployed via unknown initial access vectors. It functions as an early-stage toolkit for persistent access and reconnaissance, with overlaps in activity with GreyEnergy and Prestige ransomware. The malware drops and launches itself on victim machines, collects system information, and communicates with threat actors.

indicators.context: The malware, which we are calling "Kapeka", is a flexible backdoor with all the necessary functionalities to serve as an early-stage toolkit for its operators.

title: ScreenConnect - SlashAndGrab Exploitation Indicators
rules_yaml:
title: ScreenConnect Initial Access via CVE-2024-1709/CVE-2024-1708
id: 5a3f0c6e-2b5d-4e8a-9f1c-1a2b3c4d5e6f
status: experimental
description: Detects unauthenticated HTTP POST requests to ScreenConnect endpoint that exploit CVE-2024-1709 and CVE-2024-1708 for path traversal and authentication bypass to create privileged accounts.
references:
    - https://www.huntress.com/blog/slashandgrab-screen-connect-post-exploitation-in-the-wild-cve-2024-1709-cve-2024-1708
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-09-24
tags:
    - attack.initial_access
logsource:
    category: webserver
    product: apache
    service: ScreenConnect
detection:
    selection:
        cs-method: POST
        cs-uri-query: /
        cs-uri-stem: /
    keywords:
        request_body|contains:
            - 'path traversal'
            - 'create privileged account'
    condition: all of selection and keywords
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative scripts using ScreenConnect API
level: high

rules_yaml:
title: Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect CVE-2024-3400 Initial Access via Command Injection
id: 5a8f1c9d-7b2e-4a6f-9c1d-8e2f3a4b5c6d
status: experimental
description: Detects initial access attempt to Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS GlobalProtect service via unauthenticated HTTP POST request with crafted SESSID cookie containing directory traversal and command injection payload.
references:
    - https://security.paloaltonetworks.com/CVE-2024-3400
    - https://labs.watchtowr.com/palo-alto-putting-the-protecc-in-globalprotect-cve-2024-3400/
    - https://attackerkb.com/topics/SSTk336Tmf/cve-2024-3400/rapid7-analysis
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1210/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-09-24
tags:
    - attack.initial-access
    - attack.privilege-escalation
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.t1210
logsource:
    category: webserver
    product: linux
    service: nginx
detection:
    selection:
        cs-method: POST
        cs-uri-query: /global-protect/login.esp
        cs-cookie|contains: 'SESSID='
        cs-cookie|regex: 'SESSID=.*\.{2}\/.*'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative access using valid session IDs
level: high

title: Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect CVE-2024-3400 Command Execution via Telemetry
id: 30661d99-0ac0-49ae-92f2-8f787beafe91
status: experimental
description: Detects command execution via curl command injection in telemetry functionality after exploitation of CVE-2024-3400.
references:
    - https://security.paloaltonetworks.com/CVE-2024-3400
    - https://labs.watchtowr.com/palo-alto-putting-the-protecc-in-globalprotect-cve-2024-3400/

    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/007/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1068/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-09-24
tags:
    - attack.execution
    - attack.privilege-escalation
    - attack.t1059.007
    - attack.t1068

    category: process_creation
    product: linux
    service: sysmon
detection:
    selection:
        Image|endswith: '/dt_curl'
        CommandLine|contains: 'curl'
        CommandLine|contains: '--data-binary'
        CommandLine|contains: '@'
        CommandLine|regex: 'curl.*--data-binary.*@.*'
    condition: selection

    - Legitimate telemetry collection processes using curl with data files
level: high

title: Potential Exploitation of CVE-2024-37085 - Suspicious ESX Admins Group Activity
rules_yaml:
title: ESXi Admin Group Creation or Modification via Net Command
id: e1feaf1b-e679-4107-aa3a-bd37aac87d8f
status: experimental
description: Detects creation or modification of the 'ESX Admins' group using the 'net group' command, indicating privilege escalation via CVE-2024-37085.
references:
    - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2024/07/29/ransomware-operators-exploit-esxi-hypervisor-vulnerability-for-mass-encryption/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1548/001/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-09-24
tags:
    - attack.privilege_escalation
    - attack.initial_access
    - attack.t1078.002
    - attack.t1548.001
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'net group "ESX Admins" /domain /add'
            - 'net group "ESX Admins" username /domain /add'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative scripts creating or modifying domain groups
level: high

attack_vector.attacker_controlled_input: Group name 'ESX Admins' and user membership

rules_yaml:
title: Raspberry Robin Initial Access via Infected USB Drive
id: 5a2b3c4d-5a2b-5a2b-5a2b-5a2b3c4d5e6f
status: experimental
description: Detects initial access via infected USB drive containing LNK file disguised as a folder, which triggers execution via autorun.inf or user interaction.
references:
    - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2022/10/27/raspberry-robin-worm-part-of-larger-ecosystem-facilitating-pre-ransomware-activity/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/003/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/001/

date: 2026-09-24

    - attack.t1078.001

    category: file_event
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetFilename|contains: '\recovery.lnk'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate software installation files named recovery.lnk
level: high

title: Raspberry Robin Execution via cmd.exe and msiexec.exe
id: 6b3c4d5e-6b3c-6b3c-6b3c-6b3c4d5e6f70
status: experimental
description: Detects execution of malicious code using cmd.exe to launch msiexec.exe, which is a common Raspberry Robin technique for installing payloads.
references:
    - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2022/10/27/raspberry-robin-worm-part-of-larger-ecosystem-facilitating-pre-ransomware-activity/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/003/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1218/007/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-09-24
tags:
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1059.003
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_cmd:
        Image|endswith: '\cmd.exe'
        CommandLine|contains: 'msiexec.exe'
    condition: selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative scripts using cmd.exe to call msiexec.exe
level: high

title: Raspberry Robin Persistence via RunOnce Registry Key
id: 7c4d5e6f-7c4d-7c4d-7c4d-7c4d5e6f7081
status: experimental
description: Detects persistence mechanism using the RunOnce registry key, which is a common Raspberry Robin technique for maintaining access.
references:
    - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2022/10/27/raspberry-robin-worm-part-of-larger-ecosystem-facilitating-pre-ransomware-activity/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1547/001/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-09-24
tags:
    - attack.persistence
    - attack.t1547.001
logsource:
    category: registry_event
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetObject|contains: '\RunOnce'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate software using RunOnce for updates or installations
level: high

title: Raspberry Robin Defense Evasion using Set-MpPreference
id: 8d5e6f70-8d5e-8d5e-8d5e-8d5e6f708192
status: experimental
description: Detects use of Set-MpPreference to disable Windows Defender scanning of removable drives, a technique used by Raspberry Robin for defense evasion.
references:
    - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2022/10/27/raspberry-robin-worm-part-of-larger-ecosystem-facilitating-pre-ransomware-activity/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/001/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-09-24
tags:
    - attack.defense_evasion
    - attack.t1562.001
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        CommandLine|contains: 'Set-MpPreference'
        CommandLine|contains: 'DisableRemovableDriveScanning'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative scripts disabling Windows Defender scanning
level: high

It leverages autorun.inf or user interaction to execute malicious code, uses living-off-the-land binaries (LOLBins) like msiexec.exe and rundll32.exe for execution, and persists using registry keys such as RunOnce. The malware has evolved to deploy other malware families including FakeUpdates, IcedID, Bumblebee, and TrueBot, often leading to ransomware activity through follow-on attacks by groups like DEV-0243 (EvilCorp) and DEV-0950 (FIN11/TA505).

    service: http
